context_length: Single-sequence in this benchmark (E1 also supports retrieval-augmented multi-sequence context)
summary: The 300M Profluent E1 encoder; a retrieval-augmented protein LM positioned as a drop-in ESM replacement. Here it is used single-sequence, producing 1024-dim embeddings.
architecture: Protein encoder that can condition on retrieved homologous sequences via block-causal multi-sequence attention; in this benchmark it is run single-sequence to produce 1024-dim per-residue embeddings.
pretraining_data: ≈4 trillion tokens from the Profluent Protein Atlas.
pretraining_objective: Encoder pretraining with retrieval augmentation (conditioning on homologous sequences).
key_innovations: Explicit retrieval augmentation: integrates evolutionary context at inference via multi-sequence attention
Reported state-of-the-art zero-shot fitness and unsupervised contact prediction; drop-in ESM replacement
when_to_use: As a modern ESM-style encoder; note that its headline retrieval-augmentation advantage is not exercised here (single-sequence embeddings only).
caveats: Very recent (2025 preprint); much of its benefit comes from retrieval context that this benchmark does not supply. Verify per-size architecture details before quoting.
